newsitem.title: USA: U.S. August farm prices down 1.7 pct from July.
newsitem.headline: U.S. August farm prices down 1.7 pct from July.

text.p: Farm prices fell 1.7 percent in August from July, largely because of a drop in wheat prices, the Agriculture Department said Friday.
However, the All Farm Products Index of prices paid to farmers showed farm prices were still well above last year's level, with the August index 14 percent higher than a year ago.
Prices for wheat, while still 7 percent up from last year, were down 5.0 percent from July at $4.51 a bushel, the department said.
The decline in wheat more than offset record highs for corn, which rose to $4.50 a bushel in August from $4.43 in July. Farmers received $2.63 a bushel for corn in August 1995.
The overall index was measured at 116 percent of its 1990-92 base, compared with 118 percent in July and 102 percent in August last year.

Livestock and livestock products prices were unchanged in August from July, but 12 percent higher than a year earlier. Cattle, hog, milk, broiler and egg prices were up from last month, while turkey prices were down.

The August hog price, at $59.80 per hundredweight, was up $1.10 from July and $11.20 above last year. Strong bacon demand by fast-food restaurants was largely responsible for the increase in the price of pork bellies.

The August beef cattle price, at $60.80 per hundredweight, was up $1.90 from July and up $1.40 from a year ago. Tighter fed beef supplies and purchases for Labour Day specials have pushed prices to yearly highs.

Milk prices rose 40 cents in August from last month, to $15.70 per hundredweight, compared with $12.40 a year ago. Milk supplies were tight and demand for manufactured dairy products was high, the department said.
